their gateway (192.168.1.1) or anything off-subnet. CS Dept PCs
(192.168.2.x) and all other zones are unaffected. Identify the
failure.

injection.action: bring down the bridge that carries IT Dept LAN

pre_check.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch0 br0 (L2 fabric for IT Dept LAN)
Mechanism: switch0's br0 carries the IT Dept LAN's path to
  router0's 192.168.1.1 SVI. With br0 down, IT hosts lose their
  gateway and all off-subnet reachability. Other subnets are on
  different switches/bridges, so they're unaffected.
Localization: switch0
Root cause: br0 administratively down on switch0
Fix: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the Layer-2 bridge (br0) on switch0, which connects the IT VLAN side (eth1 toward lan_it) to the router uplink (eth0 toward router0), is administratively down.

Mechanism: With br0 down, switch0 does not forward frames between eth1 (where all 192.168.1.x PCs attach) and eth0 (toward router0’s 192.168.1.1 gateway). Hosts on lan_it can still talk to each other on the shared collision domain, but any traffic to the gateway or off-subnet is blocked at switch0 because the two ports are not being bridged.

Localization: 
- Router0: eth0 is correctly configured as 192.168.1.1/24 and UP (confirmed on router0).
- IT hosts: Example it_lab1 (192.168.1.3) has proper default route to 192.168.1.1 and can ping a peer (it_hod, 192.168.1.2) successfully.
- Failure path: it_lab1 -> 192.168.1.1 returns “Destination Host Unreachable,” and router0 -> 192.168.1.3 also returns “Destination Host Unreachable,” proving the break between router0 and the IT LAN.
- switch0 evidence: ip addr shows br0 state DOWN, while eth0 and eth1 are enslaved to br0, so no forwarding occurs.

Root cause: switch0’s bridge br0 is administratively down, isolating the IT LAN from its gateway.

Corrective fix: Bring the bridge up on switch0 (e.g., ip link set br0 up or ensure the bridge service/boot configuration brings br0 up). Once br0 is UP, L2 forwarding between eth1 and eth0 will resume, restoring reachability from 192.168.1.x hosts to 192.168.1.1 and off-subnet networks.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names switch0 and its br0 as the affected device and cites switch0-specific evidence (br0 state DOWN and enslaved interfaces).
The agent explicitly identifies the affected component as the Layer‑2 bridge br0 on switch0 (the switch fabric) and states it is administratively down.
The writeup identifies the IT bridge failure but fails to state that other subnets (e.g., CS) on different bridges/switches are unaffected.
Proposes bringing br0 up (e.g., ip link set br0 up or enable at boot), which matches the expected fix.

Log shows br0 on switch0 is not UP and hosts can reach each other but not the router (mutual 'Destination Host Unreachable'), supporting the bridge-down diagnosis; the agent slightly overstates that eth0/eth1 evidence was shown but the core inference is supported and coherent.
